scope: P2 credential and account-boundary implementation. This is not full P2, P0-P11, Windows or release acceptance.
implemented: Explicit email removal sends an empty target even when a new address is typed; password verification remains required.
Credential form drafts reset on account change. Unmounted/obsolete results cannot update another account or emit a success notification.

Client and server share equivalent new-password rules across registration, change and recovery: at least eight Unicode code points and at most 72 UTF-8 bytes. Existing-password authentication is not tightened.
Security writes carry an optional expected account constraint; mismatches fail before credential mutation. Legacy clients remain compatible.
Refresh and logout constrain the shared-cookie session owner before rotation, deletion, expiry cleanup or reuse-triggered revocation. Mismatches set no cookies.
The client binds refreshes to the displayed account and refuses a different returned owner. Cold session restoration can learn its initial cookie owner.
Successful password change clears the revoked local session without sending another cookie logout. A late logout result cannot clear a newer login.
Network failures preserve credential fields and permit retry. Password recovery requires a success envelope, not merely the absence of error text.
